newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Upbeat Estonian share market extends gains.
newsitem.headline: Upbeat Estonian share market extends gains.

text.p: Shares in the Baltic state of Estonia continued their mini-boom on Monday, with the Tallinn stock exchange index climbing more than three percent in healthy activity.
The index put in its highest daily rise since the stock exchange began operations at the end of May.
It rose 3.54 percent to 104.26, continuing last week's positive trend, on turnover of 11 million kroons.
"The market is moving up and this will continue until the end of the year," said Tallinna Pank dealer Toomas Tsopp.
Hansapank led the market on volume of 3.4 million kroons as it continued to power away from the key 100-kroon mark. It ended at 107.5 kroons after Friday's 103 kroon close.
Savings Bank had volume of 2.5 million kroons and it closed at 37.40 kroons, versus 36.25 kroons.
Union Bank said earlier on Monday that its January-August pre-tax profit was 36.8 million Estonian kroons and that full-year 1996 profits would be 56 million kroons.
Union Bank had turnover of 1.3 million kroons and closed at 22.35 kroons versus 22.20.
Fourth-largest bank Tallinna Pank announced after the market closed a nine-month retained profit of 37.5 million kroons.
Savings Bank dealer Charlie Viikberg said it was now obvious that Tallinna Pank would make more than the forecast 50 million kroon profit this year.
The free market had volume of 5.5 million kroons and shares in the Rakvere meat factory were the most active on 2.3 million kroons as it closed at 4.60 kroons versus 4.25.
